pr_title: Add timeout and cancellation check to rescore phase
pr_body:
This adds cancellation checks to rescore phase. This cancellation checks for the parent task being cancelled and for timeout checks.

The assumption is that rescore is always significantly more expensive than a regular query, so we check for timeout as frequently as the most frequent check in ExitableDirectoryReader.

For LTR, we check on hit inference. Maybe we should also check for per feature extraction?

For QueryRescorer, we check in the combine method.

closes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/114955

issue_context.title: Provide a way for rescore to periodically check for timeouts/cancellation
issue_context.body:
### Description

Plugin authors and us may be doing a ton of heavy compute work in rescore. However, there is no simple way to check if the original caller is still listening (e.g. did the parent task get cancelled), or if the search has timed out. 

We should provide a way to periodically check for cancellations and timeout. Additionally we should add such checks to our more compute intensive rescoring. 

 - [x] Add ability to check if the request should be cancelled or timedout
 - [x] Add periodic checks for the QueryRescorer when it scores documents (this might be slightly difficult and require us to wrap some Lucene related things).
 - [x] Adjust `LearningToRankRescorer` to periodically check for this during is run
comments:
I am thinking one way to do this is to add something to `RescoreContext` something that Elasticsearch can call outside of the plugins and provide an `cancellationSupplier` check. Basically, the same thing that is sitting in `ContextIndexSearcher`

`RescoreContext::setCancellationCheck(Runnable checkIsCancelled)`

Then `RescoreContext::isCancelled()` can check if something is cancelled or not periodically during its compute.

I don't know if there is anyway for ES to interject its checks directly for rescore.

For example QueryRescorer should get cancelled already since it will read from the ExitableDirectoryReader. 

But LearnToRankRescorer could do a bunch of unnecessary compute if the caller is no longer listening.
Could we periodically check for cancellations after rescoring each document in QueryRescorer? We could perform this check in the `combine` method.

review_comments: Using a timeout here can be flaky. Could we use CountDownLatch and task cancellation instead? Also, we can define ScoreFunctionSpec in `SearchPlugin#getScoreFunctions()` to simulate the plugin in question.

@dnhatn I don't know how to do a countdown latch as this test could serialize. I can add an entirely new suite of tests if we want, but I thought it prudent to get a real integration test in to verify search responses are what we expect (this shows some bugs in my original approach).
